text: D4a-05 first run read (out/_analysis/d4a05_tree.json, read before this line). Top: silhouette at k = 4 to 8 is 0.0129, 0.0194, 0.0230, 0.0277, 0.0296 against null 95th percentiles 0.0107, 0.0088, 0.0090, 0.0084, 0.0074; bootstrap stability (adjusted Rand) 0.122, 0.138, 0.155, 0.171, 0.182. By the logged rule k = 8 (best silhouette; its stability is below 0.5, and k = 8 is also the most stable). Sizes 152, 119, 103, 88, 83, 69, 42, 28 (ratio 5.43). Every form has an over-represented fourth-order node in a third or more of its members, so none is broad by rule (6). Below the forms the column-permutation null passed all 70 splits it tested; every stop came from size. It therefore does not tell a split from noise. Amendment to rule (7), made after seeing this output and applying to the levels below the forms: a split is kept only if it also passes Hennig's (2007) clusterwise bootstrap stability, 100 resamples of the node's rooms (seed 4), Ward bisection of each, each half's mean best-match Jaccard 0.6 or more ('patterns', in Hennig's reading; 0.75 and above 'stable'). The same clusterwise Jaccard is computed for the eight top forms and reported, not used to choose. The top cut is unchanged.
